issues.description: The UML/problem statement defines RollerCoaster.numberOfLoopings as an int and requires constructors to accept attributes with the same types and order. In the solution, RollerCoaster's constructor signature is declared as RollerCoaster(String name, char abbreviation, double numberOfLoopings) and casts the double to int. This deviates from the specification: the constructor parameter type should be int. Students following the UML and task instructions (expecting an int parameter) would be confused and may implement a constructor signature that does not match the solution; automated checks expecting an int parameter would fail.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the RollerCoaster constructor parameter type match the UML/problem statement by changing the constructor to accept an int for numberOfLoopings (public RollerCoaster(String name, char abbreviation, int numberOfLoopings)) and assign it directly to the int field (remove the double parameter and cast). Alternatively, if the intention was to use double, update the UML/problem statement and task text to specify double for numberOfLoopings — but prefer changing the constructor to int to match the UML and task requirements.
